sites.name: Glassyard Commons
sites.program_note: The project was already in development (it appeared in permit filings in January 2026). Mayor Wilson's Executive Order 2026-09, signed Nov. 3, directs 2026 funding to speed up its opening, according to the Mayor's office and press reports.
sites.notes: Opening date changed. In September LIHI said mid-November. On Nov. 3 HSD Director Tanya Kim said it opens at the end of November. At an Oct. 28 neighborhood meeting an HSD staffer said "right around Thanksgiving". Only the month is known, so the expected date stays on the 15th. Space counts differ by source: most say 72 RV spaces and 20 tiny houses. HSD and KOMO give 92 total spaces. An Oct. 28 meeting report gives 70 RV spaces plus 20 tiny houses. LIHI says it will serve about 140 people. Wilson says the city has had no operating RV safe lot for over a year and a half.

events.title: Wilson vetoes RV permit bill, signs four others
events.detail: Mayor Wilson vetoed CB 121283, the RV permit program in Councilmember Strauss's Vehicle Resident Assistance Program (VRAP). She signed the other four ordinances in the package. One of them, CB 121279, widens the authority of the Finance and Administrative Services director to sign leases and open safe lots, storage sites and other resources for vehicle residents. Her veto letter cites the cost and complexity of a one-time census, legal issues around proof of ownership and impoundment, and storage costs. It is her first veto. Council has up to 30 days to override, and six votes are needed. The bill passed 6–3 per KING 5, The Stranger and Capitol Hill Seattle.

events.title: Executive Order 2026-09 on vehicle residents and RVs
events.detail: Mayor Wilson signed Executive Order 2026-09. It directs outreach and services for people living in vehicles, including connections to safe lots, RV storage and shelter. It directs the Human Services Department to deploy 2026 funding for outreach and to operate Glassyard Commons. It speeds up two RV safe lots and sets up a work group of city departments and community partners, including SPD. Press reports describe the work group as running 60 days. The Mayor said the proposed 2027–28 budget funds two safe lots expected to serve 182 vehicle residents. It includes $3.5M for a second lot, which has no date or location. Wilson told The Center Square that what changes in enforcement is "to be determined."

events.title: Council budget chair releases 2027–28 Balancing Package
events.detail: Budget Chair Dan Strauss released the Balancing Package for the 2027–28 budget. The council release says it protects funding to expand shelter and housing for people experiencing homelessness. It also says it fully funds the Vehicle Resident Assistance Program, including a second new safe lot. The package includes $250,000 in 2028 (HSD-021-B) for an operational and siting plan for a veterans' shelter and services campus in West Seattle. That item has no site, unit count or date. The package is not final, and committee voting follows.

events.title: Strauss says he will seek a vote to override the RV permit veto
events.detail: Councilmember Strauss said he plans to ask for a vote to override the Mayor's veto of the RV permit bill. KOMO reports an override needs six councilmembers voting yes within 30 days of the veto. The Charter window for considering an override runs from 5 to 30 days after the veto. The Center Square reports the bill passed 6-3 in October. The Stranger reports that Councilmember Saka's reversal, together with the three progressive members, would be enough to sustain the veto. As of Nov. 5-6 no override vote had been reported.

events.title: Council Balancing Package funds a second RV safe lot
events.detail: The council budget chair's Balancing Package fully funds the Vehicle Resident Assistance Program, including a second new safe lot. The Center Square puts the package's spending above the mayor's proposal at about $7.12M for an RV safe lot. The mayor's proposed budget had $3.5M for the second lot. A Center Square report on the executive order says it sets no opening date for the second lot. HSD Director Tanya Kim said the city is accelerating plans to open the second lot in 2027. The package is an initial proposal. The council's final budget vote is expected in late November.
